practice.prompt: Which is an experiment? A assign a new study method, B observe existing study habits, C review old grades.
practice.solution: An experiment deliberately assigns an explanatory treatment.

practice.prompt: In an experiment testing a tutoring program, what is the response variable? A assigned tutor, B test score, C room number.
practice.solution: Test score is the measured outcome.

practice.prompt: Why randomly assign participants to treatment groups? A balance potential confounders on average, B guarantee equal outcomes, C ensure population representativeness.
practice.solution: Random assignment tends to distribute lurking factors between groups.

practice.prompt: Researchers assign fertilizer types to plots. Is this A an experiment, B an observational study, C a census?
practice.solution: The researchers actively assign the treatments.

practice.prompt: What is the control group? A the group with most participants, B the group measured first, C the group receiving standard or no treatment.
practice.solution: A control group provides the baseline comparison.

practice.prompt: Which distinction is correct? A random sampling and assignment are identical, B sampling selects participants while assignment allocates treatments, C assignment guarantees representativeness.
practice.solution: Random sampling concerns selection; random assignment concerns treatment allocation.

practice.prompt: In a trial of 100 people, 50 receive treatment. What proportion receive treatment?
Treatment succeeds for 70 of 100; control for 50 of 100. Find treatment minus control success-rate difference.
Treatment mean score is 82 and control mean score is 74. Find observed mean difference.
What does a placebo help control? A expectations unrelated to active treatment, B sample size, C measurement units.
practice.solution: A placebo can isolate the effect of the active treatment from expectations.

practice.prompt: Why blind outcome assessors to treatment assignments? A increase treatment dose, B reduce measurement bias, C remove all random variation.
practice.solution: Blinding helps prevent assessor expectations from influencing recorded outcomes.

practice.prompt: A new drug is tested while the treatment group also exercises more. What is the concern? A larger sample, B perfect randomization, C exercise may confound the comparison.
practice.solution: Differences in exercise can affect outcomes independently of the drug.

practice.prompt: Treatment: 30 successes in 60; control: 18 in 60. Find success-rate difference.

A randomized experiment uses volunteers from one school. What is justified? A causal evidence may be stronger within the study, but generalization is limited, B it represents every school, C random assignment means random sampling.
practice.solution: Assignment supports causal comparison; volunteer recruitment limits external validity.

practice.prompt: Each patient receives treatment and placebo in random order. Which design? A census, B matched-pairs crossover, C observational survey.
practice.solution: The same patient acts as a paired comparison under two conditions.

practice.prompt: A trial randomly allocates 120 participants equally to three groups. How many per group?
Treatment succeeds for 80% and control for 65%. Difference in percentage points?
In a trial, 40 of 100 treated participants drop out versus 10 of 100 controls. Biggest concern? A guaranteed causation, B differential attrition may bias results, C the groups are identical.
practice.solution: Unequal dropout may make the observed groups systematically different.

test.prompt: Researchers assign two different teaching methods. Is it A an experiment, B a survey, C a census?
test.solution: Assigned treatments make this an experiment.

test.prompt: What does random assignment mainly help? A guarantee generalization, B reduce systematic group differences, C eliminate all chance variation.
test.solution: Random allocation helps balance confounders across groups.

test.prompt: Treatment has 45 successes in 90; control 30 in 90. Express the rate difference as a simplified fraction.
Which is true? A random assignment chooses a representative sample, B random sampling proves causation, C sampling and assignment address different questions.
test.solution: Sampling supports generalization; assignment supports causal comparisons.

test.prompt: In a trial, 60 of 100 treated and 45 of 100 controls improve. Difference in percentage points?
